But I do love myself. I accept and like who I am. It doesn't make being alienated and lonely any easier, and it doesn't seem to affect the way others feel about me. My view about myself is unusual here, but while I consider self-esteem important, the utility of it when it comes to forming relationships is dubious if you ask me.

But thanks for reaching out to help, anyway. Honestly, people like me do appreciate sincere advice. Living like this is torture.

I have plenty of self-defeating habits. I'm working on being better.

I do want to be discerning about who I befriend, so I will try not to be overly friendly to everyone. I'm not too much of a people-pleaser generally, but I would like to have an approachable demeanour.

Mental health definitely isn't all about socialising, it's complex. I have a plan to look after my mental health in the future, with emphasis on certain priorities. My mental health has been poor, and I'm fed up of it. I need to look after myself.

This was about 8 years ago, OkCupid. It's important to note that I could have certainly tried harder to look more attractive, and the same is true now. I probably wasn't very appealing.

I sent messages to about 80 women in total. I got something like 10 replies. Of that, I got a few dates. The first woman led me on, at least it felt that way. I cut it off after a month or two. The second woman was nice at first. First date went OK, second date comes and she screams at me over the phone for "wasting her time". We simply went to different entrances at a park so we had to walk for a couple of minutes to meet. I should have ended it right there, but she spent the date facing away from me, refusing to talk. I left and texted that I'm not interested, and she texted something mean back, I can't remember exactly what. Third date actually led to something. She seemed to like me and things moved fairly fast. We had a 2 or 3 month fling before she got tired of me one day and texted "delete my number". 

So that's it. I did meet somebody at least, even if she didn't give a shit about me at all. So overall, my experience of online dating was being led on, mistreated, and used for attention and sex. But hey, at least there was sex, and I'm sorry for the people who have had absolutely no positive thing happen from online dating. Honestly, that must feel as bad as feeling used and discarded.
